_meta.indication: SABRIL is indicated as monotherapy for pediatric patients with infantile spasms (1 month to 2 years of age) for whom the potential benefits outweigh the potential risk of vision loss

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, parallel group, partially-blinded, low-dose vs high-dose study comparing low-dose (18-36 mg/kg/day) and high-dose (100-148 mg/kg/day) vigabatrin
pivotal_trials.population: Patients younger than 2 years of age with new-onset Infantile Spasms, including symptomatic and cryptogenic etiologies
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients who were spasm-free for 7 consecutive days beginning within the first 14 days of vigabatrin therapy
pivotal_trials.result: 17 patients (15.9%) in the high-dose group achieved spasm freedom vs 8 patients (7.0%) in the low-dose group; statistically significant (p=0.0375)

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Not stated in the label clinical studies section (controlled IS study)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study with a 2-3 day baseline followed by a 5-day double-blind treatment phase (vigabatrin 50 mg/kg/day titrated to 150 mg/kg/day vs placebo)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Average percent change in daily spasm frequency during a 2-hour window of evaluation, comparing baseline to the final 2 days of the 5-day double-blind treatment phase
pivotal_trials.result: No statistically significant difference on the primary 2-hour window endpoint; a post-hoc analysis using a 24-hour window found a significant difference in spasm reduction between vigabatrin (68.9%) and placebo (17.0%) (p=0.030)

key_safety: Most serious risk is permanent vision loss (bilateral concentric visual field constriction in 30 percent or more of adults). In the controlled IS study (n=40), events more frequent than placebo included somnolence (SABRIL 45%, placebo 30%), bronchitis (30% vs 15%), ear infection (10% vs 5%), and acute otitis media (10% vs 0%). Abnormal MRI signal changes were seen in infants (21.5% vigabatrin vs 4.1% untreated).
target_moa: Vigabatrin is an irreversible inhibitor of gamma-aminobutyric acid transaminase (GABA-T), the enzyme responsible for GABA metabolism, resulting in increased CNS levels of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: VISION LOSS — SABRIL causes progressive and permanent bilateral concentric visual field constriction in a high percentage of patients and may also reduce visual acuity; risk increases with total dose and duration but no exposure is known to be free of risk; periodic vision testing is required but cannot reliably prevent damage; available only through a special restricted distribution program

rems.type: A REMS was required to ensure benefits outweigh the risks of vision loss and suicidal thoughts and behaviors; it consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, elements to assure safe use, an implementation system, and a timetable for assessments. SABRIL is available only through a special restricted distribution program called SHARE.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee was convened on 1/7/09 and 1/8/09; for NDA 22-006 (infantile spasms) the committee voted unanimously to recommend approval (23-0)

summary.text: NDA 22-006 for infantile spasms (oral solution) was granted Priority Review and the infantile spasms indication had orphan drug designation. The application was a resubmission following FDA's April 5, 2007 Refusal to File letter. An Advisory Committee convened 1/7/09-1/8/09 voted unanimously (23-0) to recommend approval for IS, and approval was granted with a boxed warning for vision loss and a required REMS with restricted distribution (SHARE program).
